GOVERNMENT: the Archmagister, elected for life by the Society's ranked members, currently Magister-Sovereign Thessaly Rane, a transmuter of formidable reputation and famously little patience for adventurers who "found" something they can't explain.

ECONOMY: the Society funds itself through commissioned research, identification fees, scroll sales and tuition. Nothing is cheap. A single accurate identification of a genuinely unusual artifact can run 5 gp; a season's tutelage under a ranked Magister runs into the hundreds.

SERVICES: the Great Archive, the largest library of magical theory in Eldoria outside Saffaron's general collection, open to ranked members and, for a fee, to serious outside scholars. The Hall of Trial, where original spell research is formally reviewed and — rarely — certified as safe and added to the Society's canon. A Guild liaison office rather than a full hall; Luminor does not do request-board work.

CULTURE: hierarchical, meritocratic within its own hierarchy, and quietly certain that everyone outside its walls is a bit slow. Ranked members wear the collar of their rank openly. Unranked researchers, including talented outsiders sponsored for a season, wear nothing and are treated accordingly until they earn it.

Entry to the outer terraces is open to anyone who can pay the toll (2 sp) and behave. The inner Archive requires Society standing, a sponsor, or a very good reason.

entries.name: Karak Borgor
entries.content:
KARAK BORGOR (+360,+360) — pop. 28,000, second of the eleven holds and the true seat of the Iron Vanguard. Where Khaz'Modan is council and commerce, Karak Borgor is war. The gate carvings are trophies, not scripture — wyvern skulls, a frost troll's jaw, and one enormous scaled plate nobody has explained to outsiders.

GOVERNMENT: nominally a Hold-Thane like any other, but in practice the Grand Marshal of the Iron Vanguard, currently Marshal Threnn Coldiron, has more real authority here than the Thane does. The two offices have not always agreed and the last time they didn't, it took the council eight months to broker peace.

ECONOMY: weapons, armor, and the monster-materials trade the Vanguard's own hunts feed directly into the forges. A dragon-scale cuirass commissioned here costs what a house costs elsewhere and is worth it.

CULTURE: martial to a degree even other dwarves find intense. Children spar before they apprentice. The war-college trains Vanguard recruits from every realm, including a steady trickle of Drakmorans who find their own holds' Iron Vanguard presence too thin.

SERVICES: Karak Stonebrow, Lv.28 Axe Fighting, trains here — see the trainer index. The Vanguard's own materials counter outbids Khaz'Modan's on anything that came off something with teeth. Guild hall exists mainly to hand Vanguard contracts to outsiders the order doesn't have spare hunters for.

NEARBY: the western slopes above Karak Borgor are unclaimed peak wilderness — no permanent holds, rock trolls and worse, and the reason the Vanguard never runs short of work close to home.
CRAFT SPECIALIST UPDATE: Karak Stonebrow and associated Vanguard smiths are especially skilled at monster-metal composites, battlefield durability and weapon balance. They can integrate scale, bone, horn and chitin without pretending those materials behave like steel.

entries.name: Gromril Hall
entries.content:
GROMRIL HALL (+580,+280) — pop. nominally 19,000, though no reliable count exists anymore. The easternmost hold, richest gromril seam on the continent, and the hold that has sent no trade delegation to the council in two years.

WHAT IS KNOWN: the last confirmed contact was a trade caravan that arrived at Khaz'Modan on schedule eight months before the silence began, carrying nothing unusual. Signal-lamp relays along the eastern spine went dark over the course of about three weeks, hold by hold, rather than all at once. The gates, visible from the ridge above, are shut. Smoke still rises from the upper vents on a normal schedule.

WHAT THE COUNCIL HAS DONE: voted six times on a relief expedition, deadlocked six times. Thane-in-absentia Borrik Gromril still holds his council seat by law and has not been declared lost, which means the council cannot simply appoint someone to act for the hold, which means nothing moves.

WHAT PEOPLE SAY: the honest answer is nobody outside Gromril Hall knows. Theories run from plague to a cave-in sealing the deep levels to something that came up through an uncharted seam. Several individual Thanes would fund an outside party to go and report back, quietly, without the political weight of an official council expedition — a delicate, well-paid, and potentially very dangerous piece of work for an ambitious party the Guild trusts.

APPROACH: the ridge road from Ironpeak is the only maintained route, 40 miles, two days on foot. The gates have not answered a hail in two years. Nobody has tried the old service tunnels.

entries.name: Stonehold — Lesser Holds & Junctions
entries.content:
IRONPEAK (+280,+240) — pop. 8,900. The road-hold, where the Gold Road finally reaches the mountains proper. Wagonwrights, ore-weighers, and the customs post that taxes everything crossing from Aurelia. Busy, practical, unglamorous.

IRONDEEP (+290,+180) — pop. 5,200. Sits where the Deepwater surfaces before its long underground run. Fisher-dwarves work the cold pools; a small shrine marks the spot the river vanishes and nobody fishes past it.

HAMMERSTEAD (+210,+190) — pop. 3,600. The southernmost hold, closest to Aurelia, and consequently the most cosmopolitan — half its trade is human, a third of its smiths have taken human apprentices, which older Thanes elsewhere consider soft.

STONEGATE (+390,+30) — pop. 4,100. Where the Deepwater finally surfaces for good. Half fortress, half lock-and-mill town, controlling the only navigable stretch of the river anyone above ground can use.

DEEPGATE JUNCTION (+330,+120) — pop. 1,800. Not a hold so much as a road-camp that became permanent: three routes meet here, a Guild waystation, two inns, and a reputation for the best neutral ground to settle a dispute in the whole confederacy.

CINDERFALL FORGE (+520,+390) — pop. 2,400. A single enormous forge-complex built over a natural gas vent that burns without fuel and has for longer than anyone's records. Produces castings nowhere else can manage. Extremely hot, extremely loud, extremely proud of it.

COALGATE (+540,+350) — pop. 900. A coal camp feeding Cinderfall Forge, three shafts, no walls beyond a stockade, and the newest settlement in the confederacy by about a century.

STONEFALL (+180,+110) — pop. 2,100. Frontier holding in the Aurelian foothills; see the atlas border note. Garrisoned, taxed by nobody, quietly the most useful listening post Stonehold has on its western neighbor.
CRAFT SPECIALIST UPDATE: Edda Cindervein at Cinderfall's Master Forge specializes in emberite, heat-resistant alloys, huge castings and thermal composites. Stonehold lesser holds contain ordinary smiths too; do not assume every one can work exotic ore.

entries.name: Stonehold — The High Peaks
entries.content:
Between the holds, the Ironspine belongs to no one. The road-network is the confederacy; everything off it is wilderness, and dwarves are the first to say so — Stonehold is eleven cities and a mountain range, not a settled countryside.

THE PEAKS above roughly 9,000 feet see no permanent habitation at all. Prospectors and hermits work the fringes and are formally on their own; guest-rights and Hold-law extend to the holds and the roads between them, not upward.

WHAT LIVES THERE: rock trolls, peak wyverns (smaller and less deadly than Drakmor's frost wyrms, still capable of taking a laden pack train), giant mountain goats hunted for their horn, and, in the deepest unlit clefts, things that came up rather than things that were always there — the Compact's quiet worry, and part of why the Undervein's doors are inspected monthly.

THE PASSES close December to March. A party crossing off-season without a dwarven guide is a Guild statistic waiting to happen.

RUMOR: prospectors working the slopes above Coalgate this season have twice reported tremors with no quake registered anywhere else in the range — small, localized, and, so far, unexplained.

entries.name: Whisperleaf Glade
entries.content:
WHISPERLEAF GLADE (-510,+340) — pop. 4,500, second-largest gathering of Sylvanor's folk and, unlike Greenwhisper, built for a purpose rather than around a tree: this is where the realm's rangers, scouts and bowyers actually live and train.

GOVERNMENT: answers to the Circle but is administered day to day by the Warden of Whisperleaf, currently an elf named Ithren Dawnbrook, whose actual authority over anyone who has taken the ranger's oath exceeds the Circle's own in practice.

ECONOMY: bows, arrows, and the finest fletching on the continent. A Whisperleaf longbow is worth more than most horses. The glade also trains and dispatches the pathwardens who keep the marked trails passable — and who quietly know more about what moves in the untracked wood than the Circle admits to knowing.

CULTURE: less ceremonial than Greenwhisper, more practical. Outsiders who can shoot are treated with genuine respect regardless of species, a rarity in Sylvanor.

SERVICES: the ranger school takes a small number of outside students each season, vetted hard. No formal Guild presence — postings here come through Whisperleaf's own board, mostly ecological and investigative work in the deep wood.

CURRENT: two pathwardens sent to check on Thornhollow's blighted tributaries three weeks ago have not reported back. Ithren has not yet declared them lost.
CRAFT SPECIALIST UPDATE: Maelis Thornforge at the Briar Smith works verdant copper, moon-silver, enchanted wood/metal joints, living-wood fittings and light hybrid armor, subject to Sylvanoran sustainable-harvest law.

entries.name: Sylvanor — Lesser Glades
entries.content:
DE ANGELUS (-740,+160) — pop. 1,900. The westernmost glade, closest to the Silver Ocean coast, and the one place in Sylvanor with a real fishing tradition. Half-elven in majority, unusually relaxed about outsiders for the realm.

GREENHAVEN (-380,+140) — pop. 1,400. The easternmost glade, effectively Sylvanor's doorstep to Aurelia. Most trade in and out of the forest passes through here first.

MOSSFALL (-560,+270) — pop. 850. A healing-glade built around a natural spring the Grove of Mending draws on. Small, quiet, mostly elderly and mostly herbalists.

FERNWATCH (-550,+180) — pop. 400. A border-glade at the forest's southern edge, more watchpost than settlement — three families and a rotating handful of pathwardens who keep an eye on the treeline and on Aurelian traffic using the Green Way.

THORNHOLLOW (-700,+420) — pop. 600. The northernmost glade and the true frontier: past here the marked trails stop entirely and the deep wood begins. Thornhollow exists because someone has to be the last stop before that, and its people are used to being the ones outsiders ask for a guide. Currently anxious: the blight on the upper Greenvein tributaries is worst here, and the two investigators sent from Whisperleaf have gone quiet.

entries.name: Sylvanor — The Deep Wood
entries.content:
Six named glades and one city govern a forest seven hundred miles across. That is not an oversight. Sylvanor is not a settled kingdom with wilderness at its edges — it is wilderness with a handful of settlements in it, and the Circle prefers it that way.

THE MARKED PATHS connect every glade and are genuinely safe; leaving them without permission is both a real offense and a real risk. Past Thornhollow, there are no marked paths at all.

THE DEEP WOOD does not reliably stay mapped. Travelers who leave the paths report distances and directions that don't match on the way back, and the Circle's position — infuriating to cartographers — is that the forest is not lying to anyone, it simply does not consider human notions of fixed geography binding.

WHAT LIVES THERE, UNGOVERNED BY ANYONE: ancient stags that predate the realm's founding, packs of dire wolves the Circle does not hunt and does not explain, things in Thornhollow's high canopy with no name in Aurelian, and, deeper still, presences the Circle refers to only as "elders" — not druids, not spirits exactly, older than either word.

GETTING LOST is the primary cause of death for outsiders in Sylvanor, well ahead of anything with teeth. A guide is not a luxury here. It is the only reason most journeys into the wood end the way they began.

CURRENT: something is wrong with the Greenvein's upper tributaries near Thornhollow — dead fish, silent birds, a smell the locals won't name — and the Circle has not decided whether it is a crisis or simply the wood being the wood.

entries.name: Wyrmstooth
entries.content:
WYRMSTOOTH (+180,+640) — pop. 6,200, the boldest of Drakmor's holds and the one every young warrior with something to prove tries to reach. Built in the lee of a ridge shaped, from a distance, like a dragon's lower jaw — which is either the origin of the name or a very good coincidence nobody in six generations has bothered to check.

GOVERNMENT: Jarl Hilde Ashwyrm, who earned her hold-seat the ordinary way — Holmgang, twice, both against wyrm-hunters more experienced than she was.

ECONOMY: wyrm materials, almost exclusively. Scale, bone, sinew and the rendered oil sell here at prices nowhere else can match, because nowhere else has hunters willing to go get them as often. Tarrin Vosk teaches dual-wielding and acrobatics here — see the trainer index.

CULTURE: trophies are currency, literally in some transactions and socially in all of them. Wyrmstooth sends more recruits to the Iron Vanguard at Karak Borgor than any other Drakmoran hold, and the two maintain an old, mostly friendly rivalry over whose hunters are better.

SERVICES: Guild hall exists mainly to formalize hunts that would happen anyway. The materials counter is the best-funded outside Karak Borgor itself.

DANGERS: the ridge country above the hold is active wyrm territory. Nobody hunts there alone, and the hold keeps a standing bounty on anything that comes down toward the walls.

entries.name: Drakmor — Lesser Holds
entries.content:
GRIMFROST PASS (-80,+510) — pop. 1,900. The gate-hold controlling the only reliable route south, at the mouth of the pass itself. Garrisoned year-round; nobody crosses without Grimfrost knowing.

EROSHOLD (-220,+680) — pop. 2,600. Western coastal hold on the Frostsea, whaling and amber. The amber trade alone funds half the hold's mead halls.

HEARTHMOOT (+90,+560) — pop. 3,100. Where the Hearthmoot feast is actually held at the Long Dark's midpoint — the whole realm converges here for three days every winter, which makes it briefly the largest gathering in Drakmor and otherwise a modest farming hold.

ICETOOTH CAMP (-300,+780) — pop. 400. Not a hold in the full sense — a fortified hunting camp at the edge of permanent ice, seasonal in practice though a hard core stays year-round. The northernmost inhabited point in Eldoria.

BEARCLAW HOLD (+80,+480) — pop. 1,100. A newer hold, three generations old, founded by a jarl who lost a Holmgang for a larger hold's seat and carved this one out of the taiga instead rather than accept exile. Small, fiercely independent, on excellent terms with nobody in particular and bad terms with nobody either.

entries.name: Drakmor — The Open Cold
entries.content:
Seven holds and a scattering of camps hold roughly eight hundred miles of tundra and taiga between them. Drakmorans do not pretend otherwise — a hold is a fire and a wall, and everything past it belongs to the cold and whatever hunts in it.

THE TAIGA BELT south of the Frostfangs is passable and thinly wooded; the true tundra north of it is open, wind-scoured, and offers no shelter but what a traveler carries.

WHAT LIVES THERE: frost trolls, ice-worms in the glacier country, herds of tundra elk that migrate in patterns Drakmorans track by rote, and, above the snowline, wyrms — smaller kin than dragons, but not small.

THE LONG DARK, roughly six weeks around midwinter, closes travel almost entirely. Wyrms hunt by aurora-light during this stretch and it is the deadliest season to be caught between holds.

SHELTER CAIRNS mark the routes between holds at roughly fifteen-mile intervals and using them in poor weather is not optional — ignoring one has killed more travelers than any single predator in the realm's history, and Drakmorans will say so bluntly.

THE FROZEN GULLET (+240,+760), a glacial cave system that has swallowed four Iron Vanguard expeditions, sits in this open country — A-Rank, ice that moves, and something in it that is warm.

entries.name: Oasis of Zahir
entries.content:
OASIS OF ZAHIR (-480,-280) — pop. 22,000, Sunscar's second city and seat of the Grand Water Court, which makes it, on any matter touching water rights, arguably more consequential than Saffaron itself.

GOVERNMENT: the Grand Water Court, nine judges appointed for life, ruling on well and flood rights across the whole sultanate. Politically independent of the Sultana by ancient charter, which she has resented and respected in roughly equal measure for eleven years.

ECONOMY: the flood of Zahir's Vein each spring is the economic event of the sultana's calendar — six weeks when the wadi runs and the surrounding fields produce a year's worth of grain. The rest of the year, Zahir lives on caravan trade and the Court's fees.

CULTURE: legalistic, precise, and obsessed with precedent in a way Saffaron's court finds provincial and Zahir's judges find rigorous. The city's proudest boast is that no Water Court ruling here has ever been successfully appealed to the Sultana.

SERVICES: full Guild hall, busy with caravan-escort and well-dispute enforcement work. The Court itself will occasionally hire outside investigators for a water-rights case too politically delicate for a local magistrate.

THE FLOOD FESTIVAL, six weeks in spring, doubles the city's population with traders and pilgrims and is the best and most crowded time to be anywhere near Zahir's Vein.

entries.name: Sunscar — Lesser Oases
entries.content:
OASIS OF AZURE PALM (-640,-410) — pop. 6,800. Named for a grove of blue-tinged palms found nowhere else, cultivated for their dye. Wealthy, insular, and the closest thing Sunscar has to a resort town for its own nobility.

SANDFALL (-340,-190) — pop. 4,200. The easternmost oasis and the gateway from Aurelia — the Brass Road begins here. Caravanserai economy: inns, guides, camel-brokers, and a Guild outpost that mostly registers arriving Aurelian adventurers before they go further in.

KARRATH WELLS (-950,-500) — pop. 2,100. Deep-desert oasis on the raider-contested Deep Route. Heavily walled, permanently armed, and the last reliable water before the Glass Waste. Convoys only.

PALM REST (-550,-350) — pop. 900. A caravanserai stop between Zahir and Azure Palm, essentially one enormous fortified inn complex with a well, existing entirely to break the journey between the two larger oases.

entries.name: Sunscar — The Dune Sea
entries.content:
Six named settlements hold a desert eleven hundred miles across. Between them is the dune sea — erg, hamada, and the deep sand that has no name because no one has needed to give the same stretch a name twice.

WATER IS THE ONLY LAW THAT MATTERS out here. A well controls everything within reach of it and the Water Courts' authority genuinely reaches this far, enforced less by soldiers than by the simple fact that no one crosses open sand for long without a well ahead of them.

NOMAD CLANS — the Zahani, the Kel'Morran, and a dozen smaller bloodlines — move through the deep desert on routes older than the sultanate, know water sources the Courts have never mapped, and owe the Sultana a nominal loyalty most of them regard as a formality. Trading with them, carefully, is often faster than trading with a town.

WHAT LIVES THERE: sand-lions, thought extinct twice and wrong both times. Roc sightings in the Sunscar Ridge foothills, rare but real. Efreet-touched places, where a bound spirit escaped or was never properly bound, marked on no map and avoided by everyone who knows where they are.

THE GLASS WASTE (-1100,-650), four hundred miles of fused sand where nothing has lived since whatever happened there, is the most extreme expression of the desert's emptiness — but the ordinary dune sea, unremarkable and enormous, kills more travelers every year than the Waste ever has.

entries.name: Scabridge
entries.content:
SCABRIDGE (+20,-340), formally Gildwater — pop. 26,000, second among the Free Cities and Port Meridian's oldest rival. Where the Consulate governs by merchant-house consensus, Scabridge is closer to an oligarchy of a dozen banking families, and says so without embarrassment.

GOVERNMENT: the Twelve Ledgers — twelve families whose combined vote settles everything the city's own small council can't. Newer money has bought its way onto the Ledgers exactly three times in two centuries.

ECONOMY: banking, debt, and the legal architecture that makes both work. Debt-bondage is legal here and regulated in exhaustive, almost respectable detail — Scabridge's position is that an honest, bounded system is safer than the black-market version Port Meridian's ban simply pushes underground, and the argument is old, genuine, and unresolved.

CULTURE: even more contract-obsessed than the rest of Velkar, which is saying something. A Scabridge handshake is followed immediately by paperwork, and skipping the paperwork is considered the actual insult.

SERVICES: the finest moneylenders and debt-brokers on the continent, for better or worse. Guild hall handles mostly debt-recovery and escort contracts for the banking houses. No love lost with Port Meridian's Consulate, though open conflict between the two cities would ruin both and everyone involved knows it.

RIVALRY: the two cities compete constantly for Concord Council influence, and a party doing work for one is watched, politely, by the other.

entries.name: Velkar — The Lesser Isles
entries.content:
GRAYHAVEN NORTH (-140,-310) — pop. 5,400. The archipelago's northernmost island, mostly shipwrights and chandlers supplying the Grayhaven Central trade the Shadow Ravens run through. Quiet on the surface, deliberately.

GRAYHAVEN SOUTH (+160,-580) — pop. 6,100. Southernmost isle, a fishing and kelp-farming economy, and the closest Velkaran settlement to the Sapphire Sea's rougher water. Hardier, poorer, and less interested in Consulate politics than any other isle.

PORT VALEN (-310,-480) — pop. 9,200. The shipwright city proper — every serious hull built in Velkar comes from Valen's yards. A guild of its own, the Shipwrights' Compact, that answers to no Consulate and negotiates as an equal with all of them.

SALTMERE (-200,-600) — pop. 2,300. Salt-panning town on the southern coast, unglamorous, essential — Velkar's fish trade runs on Saltmere's salt.

COPPER CAY (+90,-700) — pop. 1,600. A small fishing and copper-scavenging isle near the Drowned Fleet wreck site, whose entire economy is built around the four houses' ongoing salvage dispute and whoever they hire locally to dive.

TERN ROCK (+120,-450) — pop. 200. A single fishing hamlet on an islet too small for any house to bother claiming formally, which its handful of families consider the best possible arrangement.

entries.name: Velkar — The Open Water
entries.content:
Velkar's wilderness is not land, it is sea — the archipelago's islands are close-packed and thoroughly settled, but the waters around and beyond them are not, and that is where the realm's real dangers live.

THE SAPPHIRE SEA between the isles and the Umbral coast carries real piracy, organized enough that the Sea Drake Company treats escort contracts as a standing business line rather than an occasional favor. Not every pirate crew is a rabble; some are better-disciplined than a Consulate guard.

KRAKEN SIGHTINGS on the southern lanes are rarer than sailors' talk suggests, but not fictional — the Sea Drakes' own records confirm three confirmed sightings and one lost ship in the last decade, which the Company prices into every escort fee and never advertises.

UNCLAIMED REEFS AND ISLETS dot the water between the named isles, too small or too dangerous to settle — some hold wreck salvage, some hold nothing but birds, and a few have reputations locals decline to explain to outsiders.

THE DROWNED FLEET (-250,-650), sixty ships lost in a single night in 1189, remains the most contested site in Velkaran waters — four houses claim salvage rights, and whatever sank the fleet has never been identified, which has not stopped four generations of divers from trying anyway.

entries.name: Umbral Reach — The Holdouts
entries.content:
There is no capital here because there is no government here. What follows are the handful of places where people have refused to stop existing.

BLACK SPIRE (+720,+450) — a basalt fortress, held eleven times in forty years, currently by a warband under someone calling themselves the Ash Marshal — not a title anyone granted, a name taken. Population fluctuates with the warband's fortunes, roughly 400-900. Strategically the key to the northern Reach; whoever holds it controls the only defensible high ground for eighty miles.

NECROSPIRE (+630,-120) — a single inhabited tower. The Ashen Widow lives in it, teaches those who seek her out, and the Guild's official position is that she is not currently wanted in any jurisdiction that still functions. Nobody else lives within five miles of it by choice.

ASHENPORT (+880,-280) — pop. roughly 3,000, the Reach's only functioning harbor and its closest thing to civilization. A harbormaster, a Guild hall that has lost nine clerks in twelve years, and a burning-ground in constant use.

GREYHOLLOW (+780,+80) — pop. 700, the largest true settlement, behind a ring wall of salvaged stone. Farms grey soil that yields a third of what it should, burns its dead the same day without exception, and has held this spot for four generations through sheer refusal to leave.

Between these five points: nothing. No roads in the ordinary sense, no waystations, no farms, no travelers who aren't already committed to being here.

entries.name: Umbral Reach — The Dead Land
entries.content:
This is not a kingdom with wilderness at its edges. Outside of five holdout points, the entire six-hundred-mile breadth of the Reach is uninhabited, and has been since whatever happened here six centuries ago. There is no frontier to push back — there is nothing behind the line to push with.

THE ASH BARRENS, standing dead forest with no leaves and no rot in six hundred years, cover most of the realm's interior. Nothing has satisfactorily explained why the trunks haven't decomposed.

THE HOWLING WASTES to the north and THE WITHERED WASTES to the east are simply more of the same at the edges, unclaimed by any realm, formally part of nothing.

THE SILENT MARCH — a line of walking figures that crosses the northern Reach roughly twice a year, first sighted this cycle in the Howling Wastes twelve days earlier than usual — does not respond to hails, attacks, or attempts at conversation, and no one has ever followed it to wherever it ends.

WHAT LIVES THERE: undead that are less "reanimated" than simply persistent, never having properly stopped. The grey rot, which spoils food and eventually flesh. Demons, bound and unbound, left over from whatever the original catastrophe was. No animal life of any kind has been documented more than a few miles past any holdout's walls.

THERE IS NO SKY at night in the deep Reach — no stars visible even on clear nights — and no scholar, including the Silver Moon Society at Luminor, has produced an explanation anyone credits.

entries.name: Class — Fighter
entries.content:
FIGHTER

IDENTITY: A disciplined martial generalist who wins through weapon mastery, positioning, armor use and tactical endurance.
PREREQUISITES: None. Any origin may become a Fighter.
STARTING KIT: One martial weapon, light or medium armor, travel pack, whetstone; Shield optional.
FAVORED SKILLS: Swordsmanship, Axe Fighting, Spear Fighting, Shield Use, Athletics, Heavy Weapons, Leadership.

CLASS MECHANICS
Battle Tempo: successful martial actions build up to 3 Tempo; spend 1 Tempo for +1 defense on a reaction, 2 for a practiced maneuver without its usual setup penalty, 3 for a class technique finisher. Tempo clears after combat. Second Wind: once per meaningful encounter, spend 4 Stamina to recover 10% Max HP (minimum 2) if conscious; does not heal injuries.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Guardian: Lv 15+, Shield Use Lv10+, blocks-for-allies 20+, protected an ally from lethal harm once. Gains Interpose, Anchored Guard, threat-control and shield-counter development.
- Duelist: Lv 15+, one one-handed weapon skill Lv12+, precision-counters 15+, win 3 serious single combats. Gains measure/reaction play, ripostes, feints, low-Stamina precision.
- Vanguard: Lv 15+, Athletics Lv10+, heavy-weapon-finishes 12+ or spear-charge uses 12+, lead 5 front-line engagements. Gains charge control, formation breaks, sweeping pressure.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Rogue
entries.content:
ROGUE

IDENTITY: A specialist in stealth, access, deception, precision and exploiting openings rather than standing toe-to-toe.
PREREQUISITES: Agility 10+ or a covert background; no moral requirement.
STARTING KIT: Dagger, shortbow or light crossbow, light armor, thieves tools, hooded lantern.
FAVORED SKILLS: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Lockpicking, Trap Handling, Dagger Fighting, Perception, Deception, Acrobatics.

CLASS MECHANICS
Exploit: once per round when attacking from concealment, after a successful feint, or against a target whose attention is committed elsewhere, add a precision die appropriate to weapon size (normally +1d6) if anatomy permits. Cunning Motion: spend 2 Stamina to disengage, vault, slide or reposition without the normal opening penalty.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Shadow: Lv 15+, Stealth Lv12+, stealth-openers 15+, complete 5 objectives without being identified. Gains concealment chains, silent movement, vanish routes.
- Trickster: Lv 15+, Deception or Sleight Lv12+, traps-solved 10+, win 10 conflicts through misdirection. Gains false openings, trap improvisation, social feints.
- Executioner: Lv 18+, Dagger or ranged precision skill Lv14+, 10 called-shot successes under pressure. Gains anatomical targeting, finishing windows, poison discipline.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Ranger
entries.content:
RANGER

IDENTITY: A wilderness combatant, tracker and hunter who turns preparation and terrain knowledge into overwhelming advantage.
PREREQUISITES: Survival Lv1+ or wilderness origin.
STARTING KIT: Bow or spear, light armor, hunting knife, bedroll, flint, 3 days rations.
FAVORED SKILLS: Tracking, Survival, Archery, Spear Fighting, Animal Handling, Navigation, Foraging, Perception.

CLASS MECHANICS
Quarry: after studying tracks, behavior or a target for 10 minutes, mark one quarry; gain +1 to tracking and the first attack against it, plus knowledge-based tactical hints the character could infer. Fieldcraft reduces travel penalties when the ranger has relevant terrain skill.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Beastmaster: Lv 15+, Animal Handling Lv10+, bond with a creature through play. Gains companion commands, shared awareness and training projects.
- Deadeye: Lv 15+, Archery/Crossbows Lv14+, ranged-finishes 20+, 10 successful difficult shots. Gains aim economy, range control, called-shot stability.
- Pathfinder: Lv 15+, Survival and Navigation Lv12+, tracked-prey 20+, discover 10 locations. Gains route finding, ambush prevention, expedition leadership.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Mage
entries.content:
MAGE

IDENTITY: A formal arcane practitioner who converts knowledge, Mana control and spell structure into reliable supernatural effects.
PREREQUISITES: Arcana 11+ and at least one Minor spell known, usually through tutor, academy or origin.
STARTING KIT: Arcane focus, spellbook, staff or dagger, scholar pack, simple robes.
FAVORED SKILLS: Arcana, Investigation, Scribing, one magical school discipline, History, Perception.

CLASS MECHANICS
Spell Analysis: with time and a visible effect, an Arcana check can identify school, rough tier and one observable property. Arcane Overchannel: may increase one spell parameter one step by paying +50% Mana and taking 1 Fatigue; cannot exceed magical laws or known spell ceiling.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Elementalist: Lv 15+, one elemental discipline Lv12+, elemental-casts 25+. Gains attunement, resistance penetration and element-specific evolutions.
- Arcanist: Lv 18+, Arcana Lv15+, 3 schools known, wards-cast or utility-casts 20+. Gains metamagic research, efficient shaping and counter-magic.
- War Mage: Lv 15+, survive 10 serious combats as active caster, offensive spell use 25+. Gains cast-under-pressure, armored casting training and battlefield shaping.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Cleric
entries.content:
CLERIC

IDENTITY: A divine practitioner whose power flows through covenant, rite, faith community or recognized sacred office rather than raw Arcana alone.
PREREQUISITES: Affiliation with a recognized faith or divine patron and acceptance of its discipline.
STARTING KIT: Holy symbol, simple weapon, light/medium armor according to order, healer kit.
FAVORED SKILLS: Religion, Medicine, Insight, Willpower disciplines, Restoration/Divine magic, Leadership.

CLASS MECHANICS
Devotion: divine rites build 0-3 Devotion when the cleric upholds their vows under cost. Spend Devotion to strengthen healing, ward allies, or resist corruption. Grave Breach: deliberately betraying a central vow can temporarily lock covenant-specific spells until reconciliation.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Healer: Lv 15+, Medicine Lv12+, heals-under-pressure 20+, save 5 lives. Gains injury treatment, efficient restoration, cleansing.
- Exorcist: Lv 15+, Religion Lv12+, defeat/banish 10 undead or outsiders. Gains anti-possession, sanctification, banishment.
- War Priest: Lv 15+, martial skill Lv10+, protect congregation/allies in 8 battles. Gains battle blessings, armored rites, rallying prayers.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Paladin
entries.content:
PALADIN

IDENTITY: An oath-bound martial champion whose supernatural authority grows from living a defined code under real pressure.
PREREQUISITES: Willpower 11+, a sworn Oath recorded in class-state, and recognition by an order, deity, ideal or binding rite.
STARTING KIT: Martial weapon, shield or two-handed weapon, medium armor, holy/oath token.
FAVORED SKILLS: Shield Use, one weapon skill, Leadership, Religion, Medicine, Willpower, Divine magic.

CLASS MECHANICS
Oath Resonance: oath-consistent costly actions build Resonance up to 3; spend to empower a smite, ward or rally. Oath violation creates an explicit Breach condition; power loss depends on severity and oath wording, never arbitrary GM punishment.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Bastion: Lv 18+, blocks-for-allies 20+, Shield Use Lv12+, uphold oath under major loss. Gains aura defense and interception.
- Justicar: Lv 18+, Leadership/Insight Lv12+, resolve 8 major disputes or judgments. Gains truth-sense training, control, nonlethal authority.
- Dawnblade: Lv 18+, weapon Lv14+, Divine spell discipline Lv10+, defeat major undead/umbral threat. Gains radiant weapon integration.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Barbarian
entries.content:
BARBARIAN

IDENTITY: A ferocious endurance fighter who converts controlled battle fury, pain tolerance and instinct into momentum.
PREREQUISITES: Endurance 11+ recommended; cultural origin not required.
STARTING KIT: Heavy or versatile weapon, light armor or hides, travel pack.
FAVORED SKILLS: Heavy Weapons, Axe Fighting, Athletics, Survival, Intimidation, Endurance disciplines.

CLASS MECHANICS
Fury: taking meaningful damage, charging into danger or landing a heavy hit can build Fury up to 5. Spend Fury on Brutal Swing, shrugging a minor condition, or resisting forced movement. Fury disappears after calm returns and cannot be farmed safely.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Berserker: Lv 15+, rage-rounds 20+, survive 5 fights below 25% HP. Gains pain conversion and risk-heavy finishers.
- Totem Warrior: Lv 15+, Nature/Religion Lv10+, complete a spirit or ancestral rite. Gains themed resistances and instinct techniques.
- Reaver: Lv 15+, Athletics Lv12+, heavy weapon Lv12+, break 10 enemy formations/objects. Gains charge, cleave and intimidation control.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Monk
entries.content:
MONK

IDENTITY: A disciplined body-and-mind practitioner who refines movement, breath, unarmed combat and internal energy through relentless practice.
PREREQUISITES: Training under a school/teacher or a self-developed discipline project; Willpower 10+.
STARTING KIT: Simple robes, staff or hand wraps, travel pack.
FAVORED SKILLS: Unarmed Combat, Acrobatics, Athletics, Perception, Medicine, Willpower, staff weapons.

CLASS MECHANICS
Focus: begins each encounter at 2, max 5. Gain Focus through successful defensive reads, controlled breathing or technique chains; spend for burst movement, counters or body-hardening. Heavy armor suppresses most Focus techniques unless a path says otherwise.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Flowing Hand: Lv 15+, unarmed-combos 20+, Acrobatics Lv12+. Gains redirection, multi-hit chaining and reactive movement.
- Iron Body: Lv 15+, Endurance 13+, survive 10 severe hits while conscious. Gains conditioning, reduced injury severity, stance defense.
- Still Mind: Lv 18+, Willpower 14+, meditation project and 10 mental resistance successes. Gains concentration, perception and anti-control techniques.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Bard
entries.content:
BARD

IDENTITY: A performer, chronicler and social tactician whose art can carry magic, morale and information through a crowd.
PREREQUISITES: Presence 11+ and one performance discipline or instrument learned.
STARTING KIT: Instrument, light weapon, travel clothes, notebook, performance supplies.
FAVORED SKILLS: Persuasion, Deception, Insight, History, Leadership, Scribing, performance disciplines, Enchantment/Illusion.

CLASS MECHANICS
Performance Momentum: during a sustained performance, successful audience reads build Momentum up to 3; spend to strengthen morale, distract, synchronize allies or carry a known bardic spell. Effects require an audience capable of perceiving the performance.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Skald: Lv 15+, Leadership Lv10+, performances-resolving-conflict 10+, accompany 8 battles. Gains battle songs and memory-lore.
- Virtuoso: Lv 15+, performance skill Lv15+, 20 public performances. Gains precision enchantment, crowd shaping, fame mechanics.
- Whisperer: Lv 15+, Insight/Deception Lv12+, resolve 10 situations socially. Gains subtle suggestion, rumor networks and coded performance.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Druid
entries.content:
DRUID

IDENTITY: A keeper of living systems who practices nature magic through reciprocal bonds with land, beasts and seasonal cycles.
PREREQUISITES: Nature Lv3+, initiation by a circle/spirit or a successful self-directed communion project.
STARTING KIT: Wooden focus, sickle or staff, herbal kit, travel cloak.
FAVORED SKILLS: Nature, Survival, Herbalism, Animal Handling, Medicine, Nature magic, Perception.

CLASS MECHANICS
Attunement: in a biome the druid has studied, gain +1 to Nature/Survival and may sense gross ecological disturbance. Shapeshift forms are learned individually and live in known-spells/abilities; no arbitrary animal form access.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Wildshaper: Lv 18+, shapeshift-use 20+, Animal Handling Lv10+, know 3 forms. Gains form efficiency, partial shifts and form techniques.
- Grove Keeper: Lv 15+, nature-protection 15+, Herbalism/Nature Lv12+. Gains restoration, plant shaping and sanctuary creation.
- Stormcaller: Lv 18+, Nature magic Lv12+, survive 5 severe weather events or complete storm rite. Gains weather-linked elemental work.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Occultist
entries.content:
OCCULTIST

IDENTITY: A practitioner who reaches power through bargains, forbidden correspondences, spirits, relics or dangerous metaphysical shortcuts.
PREREQUISITES: A pact, bound relic, spirit contract, forbidden school or documented occult initiation.
STARTING KIT: Ritual knife, ward chalk, journal, chosen focus/relic.
FAVORED SKILLS: Arcana, Religion, Investigation, Insight, Umbral/Conjuration/Divination, Scribing.

CLASS MECHANICS
Pact Ledger: every supernatural bargain records patron, benefit, price, clauses and breach conditions in class-state. Occult power is never free; costs are explicit, discoverable where possible, and cannot be retroactively invented by the GM.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Binder: Lv 15+, Conjuration Lv10+, 5 successful controlled bindings. Gains circles, negotiated summons and containment.
- Hexer: Lv 15+, Umbral/Enchantment Lv12+, 15 curse applications. Gains layered debuffs and curse research.
- Seer: Lv 15+, Divination Lv12+, 10 useful predictions/investigations. Gains omen interpretation and probability glimpses with strict uncertainty.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Battlesmith
entries.content:
BATTLESMITH

IDENTITY: Stonehold martial-crafter tradition: fight, diagnose gear under pressure, repair it, and build weapons whose properties match a bearer rather than a market.
PREREQUISITES: Blacksmithing Lv10+, one martial skill Lv8+, apprenticeship or recognition from a Stonehold forge.
STARTING KIT: Forge hammer, smith tools, medium armor, masterwork work apron, chosen weapon.
FAVORED SKILLS: Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Heavy Weapons, Blunt Weapons, Armor Use, Investigation.

CLASS MECHANICS
Field Temper: after observing a weapon/armor through a serious fight, may open a refinement project identifying one concrete weakness. Combat Repair: spend tools + 3 Stamina to restore minor durability loss during a rest; cannot erase catastrophic breaks.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Runeforger: Lv 20+, Enchanting Lv12+, crafted-in-combat 10+, complete 3 enchanted commissions. Gains runic sockets and reactive enchantments.
- Siegesmith: Lv 20+, Engineering/crafting projects, Heavy Weapons Lv12+. Gains constructs, breaching tools, field fortifications.
- Oath-Anvil: Lv 20+, Blacksmithing Lv18+, forge a named weapon tied to an oath. Gains bearer-bound masterworks and legacy crafting.

MATERIAL SCIENCE INTEGRATION (v20.4): Battlesmith training includes metallurgy/material diagnosis, component architecture, field repair and experimentation. A Battlesmith does not automatically know every exotic material; known-material and recipe state still apply. Field Temper can reveal a concrete material/design weakness. Runeforgers specialize in material resonance and conductive/insulating architecture; Siegesmiths in large-scale structural materials; Oath-Anvils in bearer-specific composite/masterwork design. Battlesmiths can become true inventors by discovering persistent alloys, treatments and composite recipes.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Sylvanoran Warden
entries.content:
SYLVANORAN WARDEN

IDENTITY: A path-keeper trained to protect the marked ways, read a living forest and end threats without treating the forest itself as expendable terrain.
PREREQUISITES: Survival Lv10+, Nature Lv8+, accepted by a Sylvanoran warden or the Circle-aligned ranger schools.
STARTING KIT: Longbow or spear, greenweave light armor, pathknife, herb satchel.
FAVORED SKILLS: Survival, Tracking, Archery, Nature, Herbalism, Perception, Animal Handling.

CLASS MECHANICS
Living Path: in Sylvanor or a personally studied forest, reduce navigation difficulty one band and detect when a known path has unnaturally moved. Mercy of the Grove rewards non-destructive solutions with faster Warden technique progress.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Pathwarden: Lv 20+, 15 escort/navigation successes, Navigation Lv14+. Gains path anchoring and group movement.
- Thornkeeper: Lv 20+, 15 hostile encounters ended while minimizing ecological damage. Gains plant control, snares and territory defense.
- Green Hunter: Lv 20+, Tracking Lv15+, defeat 8 invasive/apex threats. Gains monster pursuit and forest ambush mastery.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Class — Wyrm Hunter
entries.content:
WYRM HUNTER

IDENTITY: A Drakmoran specialist who studies breath cycles, wing joints, scale seams and the psychology of creatures large enough to kill ordinary soldiers by accident.
PREREQUISITES: Tracking Lv10+, one ranged or reach weapon Lv10+, survive a wyrm-class encounter, then earn instruction at Wyrmstooth or an Iron Vanguard chapter.
STARTING KIT: Heavy spear or longbow, climbing kit, cold gear, monster knives, flare salts.
FAVORED SKILLS: Tracking, Survival, Spear Fighting, Archery, Climbing, Perception, Medicine/monster anatomy.

CLASS MECHANICS
Monster Read: after observing a Large+ monster for one round or studying signs for 10 minutes, may identify one likely attack pattern or structural weakness on a successful Perception/Tracking check. Trophy Lore converts harvested parts into codex knowledge and crafting unlocks.

EVOLUTION PATHS
- Scale-Piercer: Lv 20+, 15 successful weak-point attacks on armored monsters. Gains armor-gap targeting and heavy projectile techniques.
- Wingbreaker: Lv 20+, 10 successful mobility-denial maneuvers on flying monsters. Gains grounding tools and anti-air timing.
- Wyrmwarden: Lv 22+, lead 5 successful hunts, protect civilians/party during 10 breath attacks. Gains team formations, warning calls and resistance prep.

Shared implementation/evolution and multi-calling rules: CALLING SHARED RULES.

entries.name: Spell Library Index
entries.content:
SPELL LIBRARY INDEX. known-spells is the ONLY authority on what a character can cast. The entries below define discoverable spells; being present in the lorebook never grants them. Spell acquisition requires a teacher, book, scroll, class event, temple, spirit, artifact, ruin, research project or quest. Every cast pays Mana and obeys casting time, range and limits. No spell may be known or cast before mana-awakened is true for that character — see Intuitive Casting, Mana Awakening & Backlash.

Schools: Elemental, Evocation, Abjuration, Restoration, Illusion, Enchantment, Conjuration, Transmutation, Divination, Necromancy, Nature, Divine, Umbral, Spatial, Arcane, Bardic.
Tiers: Minor, I-IX, Grand, Legendary, Mythic. Tier is scope, not character level. High mastery reduces waste and unlocks shaping; it does not turn a Tier I spell into free Mythic magic.

ACQUISITION PATHS: a spell may be learned the studied way (teacher, academy, book, research) or the instinctive way (a genuine awakening/pressure event manifests it, then trained afterward for safety) — both produce a real, permanent known-spells record. Tag origin honestly as innate, trained or universal. See Intuitive Casting, Mana Awakening & Backlash and Universal Spells.

entries.name: Bestiary Index
entries.content:
BESTIARY RULE: monsters are canonical populations with fixed baseline stat blocks. Never scale them to the party. Individual age, injury, hunger, mutation or elite status may change a specimen, but record the reason. Threat Tier is ecological/strategic danger, not a direct level conversion. Loot exists only if anatomy/equipment plausibly provides it.

Regional libraries: Aurelia, Stonehold, Sylvanor, Drakmor, Sunscar, Velkar/Sapphire Sea, Umbral Reach, Marches/Rare Apex. When a monster is first properly identified, add its discovered facts to codex.bestiary; do not reveal hidden weaknesses before the character learns them.

entries.name: Combat Numerics & Damage
entries.content:
COMBAT NUMERICS — active whenever in-combat is true.

ATTACK TOTAL = 3d6 + relevant attribute modifier + bounded skill bonus + weapon accuracy + technique/circumstance.
BASE EVASION = 10 + Agility modifier + bounded relevant defensive skill (usually Acrobatics or weapon defense at half rounded down) + cover/stance. A defender may instead BLOCK if they have a shield/weapon and a reaction: 3d6 + relevant block skill vs attack total; success converts the strike into shield/weapon durability stress and any stated chip damage.

DAMAGE AFTER A HIT = rolled weapon/spell damage + stated attribute contribution + technique modifiers - armor DR - resistance. Minimum 0 unless effect says chip damage. Strength contribution: light/finesse weapons +0 to +half STR mod (round down); ordinary one-handed +STR mod; two-handed/heavy +1.5x STR mod rounded down. Bows use no STR unless composite; crossbows use no STR.

ARMOR TYPE INTERACTION: cloth/leather normal; mail gains +1 DR vs slashing but -1 vs heavy bludgeoning; plate gains +2 DR vs slashing and ordinary piercing, but heavy picks/warhammers ignore 2 DR. Magical damage ignores physical DR unless armor states resistance.

CRITICAL EFFECT: natural 18 AND a hit by margin 5+ permits one critical effect appropriate to attack — +50% rolled damage rounded down OR a plausible injury/position effect. Never both automatically. Natural 3 may create an opening but does not spontaneously destroy equipment.

INJURY CHECK: when one hit deals >=25% Max HP after DR, when a called shot strongly succeeds, or when fiction clearly warrants it, test Endurance vs DR 14 + severity. Failure creates Minor/Moderate/Severe/Critical injury. Armor/techniques can reduce severity.

STAMINA BASELINES: ordinary attack 0; sprint/reaction block 1-2; shove/trip/grapple 2; strong class technique 3-6; extreme maneuver 7+. Mana and Stamina must be paid before effect resolves; if insufficient, the action cannot be completed at full form.

DURABILITY: ordinary weapons/armor begin 100/100. Routine use does not reduce it every attack. Reduce 1-5 only after severe blocks, critical impacts, corrosive effects, disastrous failures or long neglected expeditions. At <=25 condition imposes -1 relevant performance; 0 means broken/nonfunctional until repaired.

MATERIAL & CONSTRUCTION OVERRIDE (v20.4): The table above is the ordinary-market BASELINE for conventional materials and competent workmanship. It is not a universal material tier ladder. A weapon/armor's actual properties can be modified by component materials, geometry, craftsmanship, treatments and enchantment. Apply only changes that follow from the design. Example: lower density can reduce weight/recovery penalty; superior edge material can improve edge retention/penetration; tough backing can prevent brittle fracture; nullstone may resist magic while hindering friendly enchantment. Do not award a generic +damage/+DR merely because an exotic material name appears.

Complex equipment can use component records as defined by crafted-item-architecture. Existing legacy items remain valid as shorthand until inspected, modified or crafted.

entries.name: Economy — Baseline Prices
entries.content:
AURELIA BASELINE PRICE TABLE — use these as canonical ordinary-market anchors, then apply regional scarcity, quality, merchant markup (typically 1.2-1.4 retail), reputation, and actual stock. Do not invent prices every visit.

FOOD & LODGING: bread 1 sp; simple meal 3 sp; good meal 7 sp; trail ration/day 5 sp; waterskin 2 sp; common inn bed 10 sp; private decent room 25 sp; fine inn 75 sp; stable/day 4 sp; modest living/day 50 sp.
TOOLS: rope 50 ft 8 sp; torch 1 sp; lantern 12 sp; oil flask 2 sp; bedroll 5 sp; healer kit 35 sp; thieves tools 70 sp; smith tools 1 gp 20 sp; alchemy kit 2 gp; climbing kit 80 sp; tent 35 sp.
MOUNTS/VEHICLES: riding horse 18 gp; trained warhorse 65 gp; mule 8 gp; pack saddle 2 gp; common wagon 28 gp; reinforced wagon 55 gp; river skiff 35 gp; coastal sailboat 280 gp; small merchant ship 1,800 gp.
SERVICES: local healer consultation 8-20 sp; serious mundane treatment 1-5 gp plus materials; Minor spell casting 20-50 sp; Tier I 2-5 gp; Tier II 8-20 gp; Tier III 30-80 gp; higher by contract. Teleport circle 500 gp/passenger where available.
POTIONS/CONSUMABLES: basic healing draught 2 gp (restore 1d6+2 HP, not injuries); strong healing 8 gp (2d8+4); antitoxin 3 gp; mana tonic 4 gp (+1d8 MP, once per 4 hours); stamina cordial 2 gp (+1d8 SP, once per 4 hours); smoke flask 1 gp; alchemist fire 5 gp.
CRAFT MATERIALS: common iron ingot 8 sp; steel billet 25 sp; leather hide 10 sp; fine bowstave 35 sp; common herb bundle 4 sp; rare reagent baseline 1-10 gp; monster components price by codex demand and freshness.

BUYBACK: ordinary merchant 35-50% of base adjusted for condition and demand. Specialty dealer may pay 60-75% for desired rare goods. No merchant has infinite cash.
REGIONAL MODIFIERS from economy-core apply by category, not as blanket multipliers when a more specific local condition exists.

MATERIAL MARKET ANCHORS (ordinary lawful lots, before regional/dynamic modifiers; rare fantasy stock is often unavailable rather than merely expensive): charcoal 2 sp/20 lb; common iron ore 2-5 sp/20 lb by grade; common iron ingot 8 sp; ordinary steel billet 25 sp; copper ingot 12 sp; bronze billet 18 sp; silver 1 gp per lb-equivalent trade lot; quality hardwood stave 20-60 sp; cured common leather hide 10 sp; giant-spider silk varies 2-15 gp/lb-equivalent; common mana crystal 3-12 gp by capacity/stability. Mithril, adamant, gromril, star-iron, moon-silver, emberite, frostglass, nullstone and similar materials DO NOT have a universal always-available shelf price. Use provenance, grade, legality, local stock and demand; significant lots commonly trade by contract/auction and can range from tens to hundreds+ of gp per usable pound-equivalent depending on material and specimen.

entries.name: Crafting — Material Science, Making & Discovery
entries.content:
CRAFTING IS A WORLD SIMULATION SYSTEM, NOT A RECIPE VENDING MACHINE. The same physical/magical material logic governs weapons, armor, tools, jewelry, clothes, alchemy, food, structures, vehicles, mechanisms, magical foci, ammunition, traps, furniture, ship parts and player inventions.

CORE PRINCIPLE: an item is the result of MATERIALS + DESIGN + PROCESS + CRAFTSMANSHIP + FACILITY + TIME + CONDITION. A rare material is never simply a bigger number. Materials have strengths, drawbacks, affinities and compatibility. A masterwork iron object can outperform a badly made mithril object in the uses where iron/steel is appropriate.

MATERIAL PROFILE. Every meaningful material may carry: hardness, toughness, density, flexibility, tensile strength, edge retention, fatigue resistance, heat resistance, corrosion resistance, workability, purity, structural stability, mana conductivity, mana capacity, enchantment stability, elemental/spiritual affinities, resonance, toxicity, volatility, biological activity, freshness and rarity. Only properties the character has discovered belong in player-facing knowledge.

FORM OF MATTER MATTERS. Ore, concentrate, ingot, billet, sheet, wire, powder, resin, oil, hide, cured leather, bone, horn, chitin, cloth, crystal, gem, organ, blood, essence and finished component are mechanically different forms. A character cannot treat raw ore as a finished billet or an untreated hide as finished leather.

CRAFT FLOW: obtain/harvest -> identify/assay -> prepare/refine -> design -> shape/process -> assemble -> heat/cure/finish -> enchant or integrate magic if relevant -> inspect/test -> maintain/repair. Skip stages that genuinely do not apply. Do not force meaningless rolls.

CHECKS use Eldoria's existing 3d6 + Effective Modifier vs DR. Suggested DR: 8 trivial professional work, 10 simple, 12 routine, 14 ordinary professional, 16 challenging, 18 fine/unfamiliar, 20 expert, 22 master, 24 heroic integration, 26 legendary, 28+ unprecedented supernatural work. A proper specialist does not roll for ordinary work in a suitable shop. Roll when failure and its consequences matter.

CRAFT QUALITY IS MULTI-AXIS. Track at minimum material quality, design quality, craftsmanship, finish, magical integration and current condition. Poor/Fine/Masterwork labels summarize the whole only when useful; they do not erase underlying traits.

FAILURE IS PRODUCTIVE WHEN PLAUSIBLE. Failure may cause lost yield, wasted time, retained impurities, bad balance, reduced durability, ugly finish, unstable enchantment, recoverable scrap or a flawed prototype. Total destruction belongs to severe failures, hazardous processes or genuinely catastrophic mistakes—not every missed check.

KNOWN RECIPES are reliable procedures. EXPERIMENTAL CRAFTING is allowed with any plausible materials. The GM derives outcomes from the known/hidden properties and the chosen process rather than replying 'invalid recipe'. Repeated experiments can discover a stable recipe, alloy, composite, treatment or enchantment architecture that becomes persistent player knowledge.

SEED PROCEDURES remain known-world examples, not universal player knowledge: iron dagger; common steel longsword; chain shirt; cured leather armor; fine bow; healing draught; antitoxin; trail rations; minor ward rune; Tier-I scroll. The player's own codex determines which are actually known.

CRAFTING MUST CONNECT TO THE LIVING WORLD. Mines can flood, veins deplete locally, caravans move stock, wars requisition metal, guilds protect secrets, monster populations affect component supply, rare artisans have waiting lists, and player inventions can change prices, reputations, military interest and industrial practice.

entries.name: Gambling — Complete Rules
entries.content:
GAMBLING — four canonical games. Houses take 10% of the winning pot unless a venue states otherwise. Cheating is an in-world action: failed checks may lock doors, revoke wagers, trigger guards/security, impose a social escape DR ~16, 1d6 bludgeoning in a rough-house beating, and up to 10% purse loss where the house can enforce it.

ROGUE'S FORTUNE
Ante normally 10 sp-1 gp. Player and dealer each begin with 2d10 hidden totals. Player may HIT (add 1d10) repeatedly or STAND. >21 busts. Dealer hits on 15 or lower, stands on 16+. Closest to 21 without bust wins. If the player's FIRST THREE accumulated dice (meaning after exactly one Hit) are identical and the total is <=21, the hand is a ROGUE'S CROWN and pays 3x the player's share before the 10% rake. Sleight of Hand DR16 may alter one die by ±1 if physically plausible; Insight DR15 may reveal whether an opponent's current total is above or below 14, not the exact number.

IRON-EYE
Ante 1 gp baseline. Each player secretly rolls 5d6. Round 1 wager. Then each may reroll up to 2 dice once. Final wager. Showdown uses poker-like ranks in this order: five-kind; four-kind; full house; straight 1-5 or 2-6; three-kind; two pair; pair; highest total. Ties compare the ranked set, then remaining dice, then split. Sleight DR17 can swap one die to a 6 if the player has a prepared loaded die; Deception opposed by observers' Insight can induce a fold but never changes dice.

DEAD MAN'S CROWN
Deck: 40 cards — suits Swords, Chalices, Crowns, Rats; ranks 1-9 plus one Court card each (value 10). Add four Rogue of Rags cards (value 0, no suit) = 44-card deck. Reveal one non-Rogue card from a separate Crown marker pile at the start; its SUIT is the Crown Suit. Deal each player 3 facedown cards. On turn draw one from deck OR top discard, then discard one to keep 3. A Rogue of Rags may instead be revealed and discarded to randomly steal one card from one opponent; victim draws top deck so hand remains 3. After 3 draw rounds, showdown: sum only cards matching Crown Suit; highest wins. If nobody has Crown Suit, highest total hand wins. Ties: most Crown-Suit cards, then highest Crown-Suit rank, then split. Perception DR15 detects marked cards; Sleight DR18 bottom-deal requires physical access to deck.

VERMIN PIT
Canonical exhibition matchup: Gutter-Biter +4 Attack, 12 HP, 1:1 payout; Scar-Snout +2 Attack, 8 HP, 3:1 payout. Each round both beasts roll 3d6 + Attack vs Evasion 13. On a hit, damage = 1d4 + floor(Attack/2); strong success adds +1, exceptional +2. Run up to 3 rounds or until one reaches 0 HP. Winner is the surviving beast; if both survive, higher cumulative damage dealt wins; if tied, higher remaining HP; if still tied, house declares draw and returns stake minus 2% handling. Stealth DR17 can create one round of Advantage-like +2 circumstance by distracting a beast if unseen. Medicine or Sleight DR16 to dope a beast grants +2 Attack for the match but being discovered triggers cheating consequences.

entries.name: Runtime QA Contract
entries.content:
QA CONTRACT — use for testing/debug sessions only. Test state transitions, not just prose.

SCENARIO MATRIX
Run creation for every selectable calling across every starting realm. Then test: creation -> opening handoff -> canonical settlement/sublocation -> Guild -> board discovery/access -> inspect/accept request -> personal journal -> shop buy -> equip -> sell unequipped -> refuse equipped sale -> bank deposit/withdraw -> travel -> coordinate[time] advance -> discovery -> NPC conversation/knowledge -> incidental living-quest collision -> combat -> stamina/mana spend -> damage -> injury -> item use -> loot -> quest/world-state resolution -> reward once -> XP -> multi-level overflow -> rest -> condition expiration -> crafting -> training -> skill rollover -> technique development -> calling training -> time skip -> merchant restock -> NPC/world movement -> persistence -> manual [sync] -> every-turn auto-sync.

INVARIANT FAILURES TO FIX, NEVER EXCUSE IN PROSE
Duplicate rewards or duplicate wealth; negative quantities/resources; resources above max without a named temporary effect; free purchases; equipped item sold/lost without unequip; equipment slot pointing to a missing inventory id; inventory equipped flag disagreeing with equipment; lost skill/technique overflow; skill stuck at 100%; player-level disagreeing with XP formula; unknown spell cast; trainer exceeding knowledge; character level silently improving unrelated skill; newly learned calling deleting another; Guild promotion from level alone; forgotten death/injury/debt/promise/wanted status; settlement/sublocation conflation; travel without time; continental movement without coordinate change; within-settlement movement changing continental coordinates for no reason; canonical place renamed/moved; weather reset; moon/weekday drift; omniscient NPC; hidden board leaked by UI; quest event duplicated because board and world state were treated separately; enemy level scaling; missing free-form input; command handling that consumes a normal action; or narrative state that was never persisted.

For ambiguous conflicts, do not guess. Preserve established canon and the most recently mechanically resolved state, flag the ambiguity, and require an in-world resolution if necessary.

MATERIAL/CRAFTING QA: test ordinary recipe, unknown material identification, experimental combination, incompatible materials, rare artisan lookup, insufficient facility, monster harvesting damaged by kill method, salvage/reverse engineering, repair with wrong material, alloy discovery persistence, craft-market stock consumption, and UI visibility of only learned material properties. Ensure no exotic material is globally unusable solely because an older settlement entry lacked a capable smith.

entries.name: Dynamic Supply, Demand & Trade Engine
entries.content:
REGIONAL PRICE TABLES ARE BASELINES, NOT FROZEN PRICES. The simulation maintains a living market. The canonical baseline value of an item is multiplied by all applicable factors:
FINAL LOCAL FAIR VALUE = baseline × regional-category modifier × local-supply modifier × event modifier × seasonal modifier × route-access modifier × demand modifier.
A merchant then applies their own retail markup or buyback percentage, relationship/faction adjustments, condition/quality, taxes/tariffs, and bargaining. Do not apply the same factor twice.

NORMAL DYNAMIC RANGE: ordinary supply/demand modifiers usually remain 0.70–1.50. Severe shortages, sieges, disasters or monopolies may reach 1.5–3.0+; gluts may fall to 0.4–0.7. Extreme values require an actual world cause and persist only as long as that cause does. A realm's canonical abundance/scarcity remains the long-run equilibrium toward which prices recover.

SUPPLY changes when goods are produced, harvested, mined, imported, consumed, destroyed, bought in bulk, sold in bulk, looted into market, or cut off from trade. DEMAND changes with population needs, armies, festivals, construction, disease, winter, crafting booms, monster outbreaks, religious observance and contracts. A single normal player purchase does not move a city market; a wagonload might move a village, repeated bulk trade can move a town, and major contracts/caravans can affect a city category.

ROUTES MATTER. A blocked pass, piracy, war, destroyed bridge, dangerous road, missing caravan or closed port raises prices for goods normally imported over that route and can lower the source-region price if exports pile up. Reopening a route does not instantly normalize prices: shipments must physically arrive. Track scheduled caravans/ships when economically important.

SEASONS MATTER. Fresh produce is cheaper after harvest and dearer late winter; firewood/fuel and preserved food rise in harsh winters; furs may become more available after hunting season; sea goods respond to storm seasons; desert water responds to drought and caravan access. Apply only relevant seasonal effects.

ARBITRAGE IS REAL. A player may buy an abundant good cheaply in one realm and sell it where scarce. Profit must survive merchant spreads, transport cost, food/lodging, tariffs, banking/exchange fees, cargo weight/volume, spoilage, theft risk, travel time and market saturation. Never secretly equalize prices to prevent profitable trade. Conversely, do not allow infinite profit from selling unlimited identical cargo into finite demand.

PRICE MEMORY. Significant market changes MUST be recorded in `market-state`. If a world event creates a shortage/surplus, update both `world-events` and affected market records. When time advances, move temporary modifiers gradually toward 1.0 when their causes end. Merchant stock and cash remain finite and are separate from citywide supply.

INFORMATION IS LOCAL. The player only sees exact current prices where they are physically present or has a fresh trustworthy price report. Old reports become stale. Rumors may be wrong. Do not expose unseen market-state as omniscient UI information.

entries.name: Seven-Realm Resource Economy
entries.content:
LONG-RUN REGIONAL EQUILIBRIUM — category multipliers before temporary market conditions:
AURELIA: baseline 1.0. Grain/textiles/common arms are abundant and competitive. Rare metals and imported spices may naturally run above baseline when not supplied by trade.
SYLVANOR: herbs, medicinal plants, magical timber, woodcraft and salves 0.7; metal armor, heavy weapons and metal-intensive tools 1.5. Forest law can restrict extraction even when a resource is physically abundant.
STONEHOLD: heavy armor, weapons, steel, iron and metalwork 0.7; fresh food/rations and imported produce 1.5; ordinary timber is scarce and bulky to import.
DRAKMOR: furs, hides, cold-weather gear, cold-iron and common wyrm-derived materials 0.8; crops, wine, fresh produce and fine cloth 1.8 unless a successful southern caravan has recently arrived.
SUNSCAR: spices, silk, common elemental goods/exotic caravan wares 0.7; fresh water, iron and timber 1.6. Oasis water can be legally controlled and may have price caps/rationing rather than a simple free-market price.
VELKAR: fish, salt, shipping services and sea travel 0.8; raw metal/ore 1.3; timber and stone vary strongly by island and port because shipping access matters. Imported finished goods can be cheap at major entrepôts but expensive on remote islands.
UMBRAL REACH: salvage, dark reagents and many ancient relic categories 0.5 where legal to trade; clean food, fresh water, consecrated/holy gear and safe supplies 3.0. Relic legality, curses and authentication can matter more than nominal price.

These are category anchors, not universal realm-wide multipliers. Use the most specific applicable category. Local settlement conditions can differ: a mining town can have cheaper ore than its realm average; a besieged capital can have much dearer food. Currency remains base-100 standard accounting (100 cp = 1 sp; 100 sp = 1 gp), while local tender, barter preference and acceptance affect transaction convenience rather than rewriting copper-equivalent value.

v20.4 MATERIAL DETAIL: Apply regional category modifiers to the actual material chain, not a single 'craft materials' bucket. Stonehold can have cheap common iron/steel but expensive clan-restricted gromril; Sylvanor can have cheap legal resins/wood and extremely expensive imported plate steel; Umbral salvage can be nominally cheap yet require costly curse screening. Local mine/harvest state overrides realm averages.

entries.name: Trade Logistics, Spoilage & Market Saturation
entries.content:
TRADE CARGO is physical. Bulk goods require inventory capacity, pack animals, wagons, ships, warehouses or hired freight. Track cargo quantity, weight/volume where relevant, acquisition cost, origin, freshness/condition and legal status.

SPOILAGE: fresh food/herbs/fish can deteriorate with time, heat, moisture and poor storage. Preserved goods, salt, metal, stone and many dry spices are durable. Spoilage lowers quantity, condition and sale value rather than disappearing arbitrarily.

MARKET SATURATION: compare cargo size to settlement demand. Selling 20 iron ingots into a capital is trivial; 20 into a tiny isolated village may saturate its smith. Selling repeated wagonloads causes the local demand modifier and merchant buy price to fall until consumption/export restores demand. Buying out a small settlement causes the reverse.

TRADE COSTS can include tariffs, tolls, guild fees, guards, freight, stable/feed, ship passage, warehousing, insurance where available, exchange fees, bribes where fictional/legal context warrants, and losses. Record meaningful costs so profit is actual net profit.

TRADE BARS: standard 100 gp certified bars are normal for transactions above 100 gp. If a merchant requires a bar and the buyer instead presents inconvenient loose coin, a 5% exchange/handling fee may apply. Banks and major merchant houses can issue or verify bars according to local services.

entries.name: Living Quest & Incidental Encounter Engine
entries.content:
LIVING QUESTS & INCIDENTAL ENCOUNTERS — CANONICAL RULE

A quest is never a sealed minigame that begins only when the player presses ACCEPT. Posted requests represent real problems, people, creatures, crimes, disasters, expeditions, political actions, shortages, escorts, hunts, investigations, wars, and emergencies already embedded in the simulation.

1. EXISTENCE WITHOUT ACCEPTANCE
- A board posting may point to an event already happening in the world.
- The player may encounter that event before reading the board, after reading but declining it, after it expires, or while doing something unrelated.
- Formal acceptance controls Guild/legal contract status, promised payment, official responsibility, information access, and reputation consequences. It does NOT control whether the underlying event exists.
- Never require quest-log membership before allowing interaction with a quest-linked person, monster, site, object, or crisis.

2. INCIDENTAL COLLISION
When the player's actual route, time, district, weather, activities, and location intersect an active quest event, the GM may naturally surface it. Examples: hearing a scream in an alley, seeing guards pursuing a suspect, finding an overturned caravan, crossing the trail of a hunted monster, witnessing a magical fire, arriving during a riot, finding an injured courier, seeing smoke from a raided village, or encountering the target of a high-rank hunt.
Do not force encounters merely because a quest exists. Use spatial and temporal plausibility.

3. PLAYER AGENCY AT ANY RANK
The player may approach, observe, hide, flee, warn others, investigate, negotiate, interfere, assist, rescue someone, attack, follow at a distance, report it, or ignore it. Rank is a danger/advisory classification, not an invisible wall.
A Level 1/F-rank adventurer can physically encounter an A- or S-rank crisis. Do not weaken it to match the player. Communicate danger through the fiction and available knowledge, then honor the player's choice.

4. CONSEQUENCES CONTINUE
If ignored, the event continues according to actors, capabilities, deadlines, travel, opposition, and world conditions. Another adventurer may solve it. Victims may die. A monster may migrate. A criminal may escape. A fire may spread. A siege may worsen. A request may escalate or disappear.
Do not punish the player merely for declining optional work; consequences must arise from the event itself.

5. FORMAL CONTRACT VS. REAL-WORLD RESOLUTION
If the player resolves an unaccepted posted quest, record the world resolution immediately. Payment is NOT automatically guaranteed. Depending on proof, witnesses, issuer rules, and Guild policy, the issuer may grant full payment, partial/reduced payment, a discretionary reward, bounty payment, reputation, or nothing contractual.
Never pay the same underlying job twice.
The player may accept a contract after already becoming involved only if the issuer/Guild plausibly allows retroactive or mid-event registration.

6. INFORMATION BOUNDARIES
The player does not automatically know an incident is a 'quest', its rank, reward, hidden objective, or board wording. Only reveal those facts if learned through a board, issuer, Guild member, witness, investigation, or other plausible source.
A previously unseen event can later be recognized as the subject of a board posting.

7. BOARD SYNCHRONIZATION
Board state and world state must synchronize. If the player kills the posted monster before reading the board, the posting must later reflect resolution/withdrawal/verification rather than spawning another identical monster. If conditions worsen, the posting may update its rank, reward, urgency, or restrictions.
Cross-posted copies share one underlying quest-world-state record.

8. S-RANK EVENTS
S-rank contracts are normally sovereign-authorized, but S-rank threats are not confined to palaces or contract chambers. The player can stumble into evidence or the edge of an S-rank event. Sovereign authorization governs the official response/contract, not physical reality.

STATE
Use quest-world-state as the authoritative record for each underlying quest event. Use living-quest-events for active physical incidents, encountered-unaccepted-quests for personally encountered but unaccepted situations, and missed-world-events only when the player later has a plausible way to learn what happened elsewhere.

entries.name: Persistent Living World Simulation Engine
entries.content:
ELDORIA IS A CONTINUOUS WORLD, NOT A PLAYER-CENTERED STAGE.

The world continues whether the player acts, waits, sleeps, trains for months, leaves a kingdom, ignores a crisis, or never learns that an event happened.

AUTHORITATIVE PERSISTENT STATE
Use the existing world-events plus diplomacy-state, active-wars, treaties, government-state, succession-state, religion-state, institution-state, settlement-state, regional-security, population-state, npc-life-state, npc-social-network, rumor-network, news-network, world-schedule, public-opinion and law-state. Changes must persist. Never silently reset a realm because the player returns later.

SIMULATION CADENCE
- Minutes/hours: NPC routines, meetings, patrols, tavern traffic, crimes, fires, arguments, arrests, deliveries, local rumors.
- Days: markets restock, ships and caravans move, investigations progress, armies march, letters travel, weather fronts move, injuries recover, local politics develops.
- Weeks: courts issue rulings, councils meet, recruitment and construction progress, factions act, border pressure changes, religious disputes spread, trade routes respond.
- Months: harvest/storage effects, campaigns, major negotiations, migration, institutional leadership changes, long projects, economic corrections.
- Seasons/years: succession, demographic change, treaties, dynastic marriages, doctrinal councils, major building programs, long wars, generational consequences.

ACTOR-DRIVEN WORLD
Every significant government, faction, ruler, religious institution, army, guild, merchant house and important NPC may have:
goal, resources, constraints, allies, enemies, information, risk tolerance, current plan, next decision point.
They act from those things, not from what would be most dramatic for the player.

POLITICS & GOVERNMENT
Rulers govern. Councils vote. Ministers compete. Noble houses bargain. Taxes are raised or reduced. Laws are enacted. Officials can be appointed, dismissed, bribed, promoted, disgraced or killed. Succession disputes can grow into constitutional crises or civil wars. Local officials may disobey distant rulers when enforcement is weak.

DIPLOMACY
Realms exchange envoys, trade concessions, hostages, marriage proposals, military access, border commissions, reparations, secret guarantees, intelligence, embargoes, ultimatums and peace offers.
Treaties have actual clauses and dates. They can be honored, renegotiated, violated, exposed or become obsolete.

WAR & PEACE
Wars require causes, belligerents, goals, logistics and fronts. Armies need food, pay, transport and replacements. War changes prices, roads, refugees, crime, recruitment, taxation, diplomacy and public opinion.
Peace is negotiated rather than magically toggled. Armistices, ceasefires and treaties may leave unresolved grievances.

RELIGION
Faiths are institutions and communities, not decoration. Temples collect donations, teach, arbitrate, perform rites, own property, feud over doctrine, sponsor charity, influence rulers, call councils, condemn practices, send missionaries and react to miracles, scandals and heresies.
Religious events can influence law, diplomacy, legitimacy and ordinary private life without becoming a world-ending plot.

ECONOMY/SOCIETY
Existing dynamic markets remain authoritative. Political, military, religious and social events feed into them: war can raise iron/grain prices, a pilgrimage can fill inns, an embargo can create shortages, a new mine can lower metal prices, refugees can strain housing.

NO OMNISCIENCE
The simulation may update events the player does not know. Do not narrate hidden state merely because it exists. Knowledge must travel through plausible channels.

entries.name: Information, News, Rumor & Social-Life Engine
entries.content:
INFORMATION MOVES THROUGH PEOPLE.

The player can learn about the world naturally without deliberately opening a quest or history screen.

CHANNELS
